answer: Like a tide that tests every hull, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a ferrous-hard stake before it may trade: the bond is escrowed, and if peers prove fraud, the stake is slashed and the identity is burned. A vine of trust then grows only between bonded agents, because each new fake identity must pay the same bond again, so a Sybil flood costs as much as the identities it tries to fake, while honest agents earn the bond back with interest.
